subject: Pilot onboarding — go-live gates & integration lanes
messages:
From: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@aurorahealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: jane.park@aurorahealth.com, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot onboarding: go-live gates, integration lanes and data residency question

Markus —

Thanks again for the RFP response. The execs liked Redwood’s approach to unified inference but before we move to SOW we need a concise pilot/onboarding plan that shows how we’ll get from PoC -> pilot -> production. Specifically we need:

- A week-by-week timeline for a 6–8 week pilot (integration milestones, test data handoff, validation).
- Clear canary gating criteria (success metrics, rollback rules, duration of canary).
- Integration lanes: what teams need to own which parts (networking, secrets/KMS, telemetry hooks).
- Any data residency or egress considerations for our US/EU clusters.

Can you provide a draft that our procurement and engineering teams can review? We’re hoping to run the pilot in mid-April.

Also looped Jane from engineering who will own the technical review.

—Daniel
CTO, Aurora Health
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, jane.park@aurorahealth.com, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding: go-live gates, integration lanes and data residency question

Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a working draft of a pilot onboarding checklist (Redwood_Onboarding_Checklist_v1.xlsx) and a short one-page canary matrix. High level notes below; the attached has week-by-week tasks.

Summary (short):
- Target pilot window: 6 weeks (kickoff Apr 19 -> pilot close May 28).
- Week 0: Kickoff, access & network validation, test dataset formats agreed.
- Weeks 1–2: Integration lanes:
  - Networking & VPC peering (Aurora infra + Redwood private endpoint) — ownership: Aurora infra / Redwood Platform Eng
  - Secrets / KMS (customer-managed keys optional) — ownership: Aurora SecOps / Redwood Integrations
  - Inference routing & model pinning — Redwood runtime 
  - Observability hooks (tracing + token-level cost tags) — Aurora SRE onboarded to console; Redwood provides dashboards
- Weeks 3–4: Canary: 72-hour baseline (10–20% traffic) with metrics observed: 99th latency, per-token cost, error-rate, output-quality (sample prompts).
- Canary gating (pass/fail):
  - Latency SLA: 99th P99 <= 450ms for 512-token median sequences
  - Error rate: <0.5% server errors / 1000 requests
  - Quality: regression <2% vs baseline prompts (we provide eval harness)
  - Operational: autoscaler scaling events <3/day during canary window
- Rollback criteria: any single gating metric failing for >12 continuous hours triggers automatic traffic shift back to baseline model + ops pager.
- Post-canary: 2-week ramp to 100% with staged percent increases and daily health checks.

Open questions we filed in the checklist: data residency zones for EU data subsets, whether Aurora will use customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed key, and preferred SLOs for asynchronous batch jobs.

Next steps:
1) Laura — please confirm SLA language and add fallback policy details in the canary matrix.
2) Monica — attach the sample eval prompt set and note on tokenization parity.
3) Daniel / Jane — confirm target pilot start (Apr 19) and provide contacts for infra/VPC peering.

Attaching: Redwood_Onboarding_Checklist_v1.xlsx (draft)

Cheers,
Markus Klein
VP, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0129
From: Jane Park <jane.park@aurorahealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding: go-live gates, integration lanes and data residency question

Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the checklist — that layout is exactly what engineering needs. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: Apr 19 works for kickoff, but we need the first 48–72 hours after kickoff to validate data mapping and do a dry-run inference on anonymized records. Can the pilot timeline be nudged one week if we hit infra delays?
- Canary metrics: we need a slightly tighter latency target for some clinical endpoints. Can you flag which APIs/endpoints support 99th percentile under 300ms on standard n1-like machines? If that’s not feasible we’ll scope those endpoints as background/async in pilot.
- KMS: procurement prefers Aurora-managed keys for now; we may revisit customer-managed keys in production.
- Telemetry: we request a prebuilt Grafana dashboard template and an event stream to our Splunk endpoint (we'll share collector details).

Attached: Aurora_Procurement_SOW_Questions.docx with a few legal/ops questions procurement wants answered before SOW.

One more ask: can you include explicit rollback orchestration steps (API calls, expected time to shift traffic, who gets paged) — procurement wants runbook-level clarity in the SOW.

Subject: Final: Pilot onboarding plan + Canary Matrix (attached)

Daniel/Jane —

Per our internal updates (Laura & Monica contributed edits), attached is the finalized pilot plan and expanded canary matrix (Pilot_Canary_Matrix_v2.pdf). Key items addressed from your notes: 

- Kickoff still targeted Apr 19, but we added a contingency week (kickoff Apr 26) in the onboarding checklist if your infra team needs extra time for peering.
- Endpoint performance: included per-endpoint performance buckets in the canary matrix. On standard n1-like machines, the following endpoints are expected to hit <300ms P99: small-text-embed, short-response-chat (<=256 tokens). Detailed perf numbers included in the appendix. Heavier generation paths remain in the 300–450ms bucket and are scoped as async for the pilot unless you opt into higher-tier Dedicated nodes.
- KMS: noted Aurora-managed keys for pilot; we’ll add CMEK steps to SOW if you toggle that for production.
- Telemetry: attached Grafana dashboard json + Splunk forwarder config snippet (see Drive link below).
- Rollback orchestration: included runbook steps — API call to cut traffic (POST /v1/fallbacks/{route}/shift), expected drift time 30–90s, automated rollback if gating metric fails for >12 hours, and human-in-loop escalation path (pager + 30-minute on-call response SLAs).

Attachments: Pilot_Canary_Matrix_v2.pdf, Redwood_Onboarding_Checklist_v1.xlsx (updated), sample Grafana dashboard (link).

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Qq-ExampleDriveLink
HubSpot ref: HS-74219

Next steps: 
- Procurement: confirm SOW Q&A (procurement@aurorahealth.com).
- Infra: provide VPC peering contacts and schedule (target: week of Apr 12).
- Engineering: Monica will share the eval prompt set and tokenization notes by Mon Apr 12.

If this looks good we’ll prep the SOW with the explicit runbook snippets and DM a DocuSign routing for signatures.

Thanks all —
Markus
VP, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
